h: Shabbat Reveals the Light of Torah

p: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים.
— And it came to pass at the end of two years.
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּתְחוּ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בַּפָּסוּק קֵץ שָׂם לַחוֹשֶׁךְ וְגוֹמֵר.
— The holy Zohar and Midrash Rabbah open this portion with “He sets an end to darkness,” and so forth.
וְכָתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: אֶבֶן אֹפֶל וְצַלְמָוֶת, דָּא אֶבֶן נֶגֶף דְּבָהּ כָּשְׁלִין חַיָּיבִין וְכוּלֵי.
— The holy Zohar says: “A stone of darkness and the shadow of death”—this is the stumbling stone through which the wicked stumble, etc.
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ: שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּצֶר הָרָע בָּעוֹלָם אוֹפֶל וְצַלְמָוֶת בָּעוֹלָם, נֶעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵי.
— The Midrash says that as long as the evil inclination is in the world, darkness and the shadow of death are in the world; when the evil inclination is uprooted, etc.
הָעִנְיָן דְּהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע עִיקַּר עִסְקוֹ לְשַׁכֵּחַ אֶת הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהָיָה אִם שָׁכֹחַ תִּשְׁכַּח וְגוֹמֵר, וְהַרְבֵּה כַּיּוֹצֵא בָזֶה בַּכְּתוּבִים.
— The evil inclination’s chief occupation is to make a person forget, as in “And it shall be, if you indeed forget,” and so forth, with many similar verses in Scripture.
וּבַגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים לב:) דְּבִשְׁעַת יֵצֶר הָרָע לֵית דְּמַדְכַּר לֵיהּ לְיֵצֶר טוֹב.
— The Gemara (Nedarim 32b) says that when the evil inclination acts, no one recalls the good inclination to mind.
וְאוֹתִיּוֹת הַחֹשֶׁךְ הֵם שִׁכְחָה.
— The letters of הַחֹשֶׁךְ, “the darkness,” form שִׁכְחָה, “forgetfulness.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 89:1: “‘It was at the conclusion of two years, and Pharaoh was dreaming: and, behold, he stood at the Nile’ (Genesis 41:1). ‘It was at the conclusion of two years.’ ‘He sets an end to darkness’ (Job 28:3) – He set a time for the world, how many years it would spend in darkness. Why did He set a time for darkness? Because as long as the evil inclination is in the world, there is darkness and the shadow of death in the world, as it is written: ‘The stone of thick darkness and the shadow of death’ (Job 28:3). If the evil inclination is removed from the world, there is no darkness and shadow of death in the world. Another matter, ‘He sets an end to darkness’ – He set a time for Joseph, how many years he would spend in the darkness in prison. When the end came, Pharaoh dreamed a dream.”

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 32b: “Rami bar Abba said: What is meant by “A small city, with few men in it”? “A small city” is the body; “few men in it” are the limbs; “a great king came against it and besieged it” is the evil inclination; “he built great siegeworks against it” are sins. “There was found in it a poor wise man” is the good inclination; “he delivered the city through his wisdom” is repentance and good deeds. “No one remembered that poor man”: when the evil inclination prevails, no one remembers the good inclination.”

h: Joseph and the Light of Righteousness

p: וּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל הָאָדָם, וְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נִבְרָא בְּיוֹם ו', שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם, שֶׁהוּא הָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם, שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל צַדִּיק א' נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם וּמִתְקַיֵּים הָעוֹלָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא לח:).

— Creation was originally for the sake of the human being. Adam was created on the sixth day, corresponding to the attribute “the righteous one, foundation of the world.” He was meant to embody that aspect, for the world was created and endures for the sake of one righteous person (Yoma 38b).
וְאַחַר שֶׁקִּלְקֵל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נַעֲשָׂה יוֹסֵף מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּמְתַקֵּן הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן.
— After Adam’s corruption, Joseph became a vehicle for the attribute “the righteous one, foundation of the world,” as is known, and rectifies Adam’s corruption.
וְכָתוּב אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק, אוֹר הֵיפֶךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ, שֶׁהוּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הַמְשַׁכֵּחַ אֶת הָאָדָם.
— “Light is sown for the righteous”: light is the opposite of darkness, the evil inclination that makes a person forget.

וּכְתִיב אוֹר צַדִּיקִים יִשְׂמָח, שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לָאוֹר זוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי הָאוֹר לְיַישֵּׁר הַלֵּב, לְהוֹרִיק הָרָע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ, וְזוֹכֶה לְשִׂמְחָה, דִּכְתִיב לְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה.

— “The light of the righteous rejoices”: through that light, the righteous person attains an upright heart, emptying evil from “the fool’s heart at his left,” and merits joy, for “the upright of heart have joy.”
וְזֶהוּ וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר יוֹסֵף שֶׁעָשָׂה קֵץ לַחֹשֶׁךְ, שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבּוֹ.
— Thus “And it came to pass at the end,” and so forth: Joseph’s refinement established an end to darkness, uprooting the evil inclination from his heart.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 38b: “Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even for one righteous person the world exists, as it is stated: “But the righteous is the foundation of the world” (Proverbs 10:25). Rabbi Ḥiyya himself said: The proof is from here, as it is stated: “He will keep the feet of His pious ones” (I Samuel 2:9), meaning that God maintains the world due to the pious people. The Gemara questions this proof; “pious ones” indicates many rather than a single righteous person. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Although the text is vocalized in the plural, it is written in the singular: “His pious one”; God maintains the world even for a single pious individual.”

This is a further virtue, in which the heart is made upright, and even the fool’s heart becomes full of holiness and the evil is emptied from it.”

h: Bread Wine and the Shabbat Meal

p: וְלָכֵן בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ נִזְכַּר שֶׁעָשָׂה יוֹסֵף לְאֶחָיו סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהָכֵן, וְאֵין וְהָכֵן אֶלָּא שַׁבָּת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה).
— Therefore this portion mentions Joseph’s preparation of a Shabbat meal for his brothers: “and prepare,” which refers specifically to Shabbat, as Bereishis Rabbah explains.

וְכָתוּב וַיִּשְׁתּוּ וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ, דְּהַסְּעוּדָה הָיָה לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי, נַהֲמָא דְאוֹרַיְיתָא דְבִכְתָב, וְהַיַּיִן הָיָה כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר שְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי, יֵינָא דְאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא עֵקֶב).

— “They drank and became intoxicated with him.” The meal embodied “Come, eat of My bread,” the bread of the Written Torah; the wine embodied “Drink of the wine I have mixed,” the wine of the Oral Torah (Raaya Mehemna, Eikev).

וְכֵן נִדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סו): תִּירוֹשׁ זֶה אַגָּדָה. וְאִיתָא בַּסִּפְרֵי (עֵקֶב פָּסוּק וּלְדָבְקָה): רְצוֹנְךָ שֶׁתַּכִּיר מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם, לְמוֹד אַגָּדָה וְכוּלֵי.

— Bereishis Rabbah, chapter 66, likewise interprets “new wine” as aggadah. Sifrei (Eikev, on “and to cleave”) says, “If you wish to know the One who spoke and the world came into being, study aggadah,” etc.
וְזֶה הוֹפִיעַ לָהֶם יוֹסֵף בְּאוֹתָהּ סְעוּדָה, שֶׁהָיָה סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת שַׁחֲרִית שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהֶם.
— Joseph revealed this illumination to them at the Shabbat morning meal he made for them.
וּבִסְעוּדַת שַׁחֲרִית אוֹמְרִים וּבְחַמְרָא טָבָא דְּבֵיהּ תֶּחֱדֵי נַפְשָׁא, שֶׁיְּכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת עַל יָדוֹ לְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה.
— At the morning meal we say, “And with good wine, through which the soul rejoices”; through it one can attain “joy for the upright of heart.”

h: Chanukah and the Light of Torah

p: וְכֵן יָוָן נִרְמָז בַּפָּסוּק וְחֹשֶׁךְ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה), שֶׁהֶחְשִׁיכָה עֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם רָצוּ לְהַטִּיל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל זוּהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ, וְהַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים נִצְּחוּם.

— Greece is likewise hinted at in “and darkness” (Bereishis Rabbah), for it darkened Israel’s eyes. The Greeks sought to introduce the serpent’s impurity into Israel, and the Chashmonaim defeated them.
וְעַל פִּי רוֹב שַׁבָּת זֶה בַּחֲנוּכָּה, וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁנֵּרוֹת חֲנוּכָּה רוֹמְזִין עַל אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַחוֹשֶׁךְ.
— This Shabbat usually falls during Chanukah. We have already said that the Chanukah lights signify the light of the Oral Torah, the opposite of darkness.
וְכָתוּב אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִבְחִינַת צַדִּיק זוֹכִין לָאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְנַז לַעֲמֵלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ).
— “Light is sown for the righteous”: by attaining the aspect of the righteous one, they attain the primordial light hidden for those who labor in the Oral Torah (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach).

וְעַל יְדֵי שַׁבָּת זוֹכִין גַּם כֵּן לְהוֹרִיק הָרָע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמְּכִילְתָּא עַל פָּסוּק שׁוֹמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשׁוֹמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע, שֶׁהַמְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת מְרוּחָק מִן הָעֲבֵירָה.

— Through Shabbat one also merits to empty evil from the fool’s heart. The Mechilta explains “who guards Shabbat from profaning it and guards his hand from doing any evil”: one who observes Shabbat is distanced from sin.
וּבִפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים הַלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל מִקִּטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע.
— Pri Etz Chaim expresses it as being saved from the evil inclination’s accusation.
וְכָתוּב מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל פְּגָם זֶה שֶׁנִּקְרָא רָע כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְעַל יְדֵי שַׁבָּת זוֹכִין לְתַקֵּן זֶה.
— It says specifically “from doing any evil,” hinting at this blemish, which is called “evil,” as is known. Through Shabbat one merits to rectify it.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 2:4: “… ‘And disorder (vavohu)’ – this is the Median kingdom, (as it is stated:) ‘They hastened (vayavhilu) to bring Haman’ (Esther 6:14). ‘And darkness’– this is the Greek kingdom, which darkened Israel’s eyes with their edicts, as they used to say to them: ‘Write on the horn of a bull that you have no portion in the God of Israel.’ ‘Upon the face of the depths’ – this is the evil kingdom (Edom), which cannot be calculated, like the depths; just as the depths cannot be calculated, so is it with (the wickedness of) the wicked. ‘And the spirit of God was hovering’ – this is the spirit of the messianic king, as it says: ‘The spirit of the Lord will rest upon him’ (Isaiah 11:2). …”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Kislev–Tevet 4:58: “‘To make them forget Your Torah’: they instituted the wording ‘to make them forget,’ and not ‘to annul them’ or ‘to nullify them.’ … The Midrash says, ‘And darkness: this is the kingdom of Greece, which darkened the eyes of Israel with its decrees.’ Since they sought to abolish the faith, which is the wisdom of the Torah, and to strengthen the external Greek wisdoms, they are called darkness, for wisdom is called light, while folly is called darkness, as it says, ‘The fool walks in darkness.’ … It emerges from all this that the entire power and dominion of the kingdom of Greece lies in the aspect of darkness, which is forgetting of the Torah. … In the aspect of darkness comes forgetting: choshech, darkness, and shachach, forgot, have the same letters. Hence you will understand well why the thanksgiving prayer was instituted with the words, ‘When the wicked kingdom of Greece rose up … to make them forget Your Torah.’”
